companyRankingLists.description: Creating a more empathetic workplace looks like staying loyal to workers, emphasizing D&I initiatives, and paying well.
companyRankingLists.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
New Jersey–based pharmaceutical company Merck climbed 36 spots from No. 98 on last year’s Best Companies list, with about 75% of the company’s employees worldwide undergoing a pay equity study as of 2021, which grew to 90% in 2022. That 2022 study, by the way, showed that Merck had achieved over 99% pay equity for both women and men and white and non-white employees in the U.S.
 

Merck’s diversity programs have worked to address gender pay disparities and representation of women in the workplace. The company’s board of directors has more gender diversity than the industry norm, consisting of 46% female representation, while women make up 33% of Merck’s executives. Merck’s Women’s Leadership Program and Emerging Women’s Leadership program provide professional development training for women employees.

companyRankingLists.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
While Merck’s business focus revolves around using science to save lives and improve physical health, the company has made the mental health of its employees a priority as well.

  • Roughly 4,000 managers have been trained on how to connect their workers with well-being resources and educated on how to respond with compassion toward someone who may be struggling.

  • Roughly 100 workers have completed Mental Health First Aid training and are available to help colleagues access mental health information and resources. It’s a grassroots project to reduce the stigma and raise awareness of mental health issues.

  • Lyra, launched in 2021, ensures both employees and their families have quick access to high-quality evidence-based mental health care.

  • Employees are provided with a membership to relaxation app Calm, as well as a flex day, time off to volunteer, and a generous parental leave program.

  • “Merck shows that we are people, not just employees, with lives outside of work and honors that and promotes balancing work/home life,” said one worker.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The pharmaceutical firm that makes commonly used drugs, including HPV vaccine Gardasil, has held strong in its 69th year on the Fortune 500 list.

  • Merck surpassed expectations in 2022, bringing in $59.3 billion in revenue and $14.5 billion in profit.

  • In April 2023, Merck announced plans to acquire Prometheus Biosciences for $10.8 billion. It is one of a few deals of its kind, but analysts say it could signal the beginning of a period of intense M&A for biotech companies.

  • Merck, along with Moderna, is making progress toward a cancer vaccine for melanoma patients. The immunotherapy drug Keytruda, Merck’s top seller, is part of the vaccine and was a strong growth driver.

  • Sales of the COVID oral antiviral drug Lagevrio reported robust sales in 2022, but the company expects a significant slowdown in 2023.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Merck’s Gardasil is a potent vaccine against HPV, a sexually transmitted disease that can cause cervical cancer. But until recently, cost and production constraints limited its reach. Merck has now committed more than $1 billion to expand capacity, with a focus on underserved countries. Merck more than doubled global supply of Gardasil between 2017 and 2020 and is on track to do so again by 2023.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Pharmaceutical company Merck fell six spots on the list in its first year with CEO Robert Davis at the helm. But that modest slide masks a successful year in which profits jumped 85%, to $13 billion. Excluding revenue from Organon, the women’s health company whose spinoff was completed in June 2021, Merck’s sales overall increased 17%, including a 20% gain for the company’s hallmark cancer drug Keytruda and a 44% increase in sales for HPV vaccine Gardasil. Merck also registered nearly $1 billion in sales for molnupiravir, an oral antiviral treatment for COVID that received emergency use authorization from the FDA in December 2021.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: New to our list this year, this 130-year-old pharma giant has long devoted itself to the mission: “Save and improve lives.” Though Merck shelved its own vaccine development, President Biden announced in March that the company would help produce J&J’s one-shot COVID vaccine. When current CEO Ken Frazier departs at the end of June, CFO Robert Davis will take the reins. Employees say that during a difficult year, it meant a lot that Merck managed to increase benefits to employees. That included the addition of “LifeCare” specialists who can provide help in hiring a nanny or search for virtual tutors to support e-learning.The company has “stepped up,” notes an employee.

companyRankingLists.description: Total revenue for the world’s biggest companies fell 4.8% to $31.7 trillion this year—the first decline in half a decade.
companyRankingLists.title: Fortune Global 500
companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Merck spent much of 2020 developing and testing two COVID-19 vaccine candidates but abandoned the projects in January. The company said in March that it would support the manufacturing and supply of Johnson & Johnson’s COVID-19 vaccine instead. Merck’s worldwide sales increased 2% to $48 billion last year, led by a 30% increase in revenue ($14.4 billion) from its flagship cancer drug Keytruda. Despite the sales growth, Merck saw a 28% decrease in net income in 2020 compared with the prior year. And the numbers in 2021 aren’t exactly flashing green—at least so far: First-quarter sales were flat, and profit declined because of the continuing effects of the pandemic as well as increased competitive pressures for key Merck products. One more challenge for the venerable drugmaker: In June, longtime CEO Ken Frazier steps down after a stellar decade-long run leading the company. He will hand the reins to CFO Robert Davis.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The pharma giant had a banner year in 2019, climbing 29 slots on the Global 500. Revenue rose almost 11%, to $46.8 billion, while profits leaped 58%, to $9.8 billion. Blockbuster cancer drug Keytruda, as well as an expanded line of animal medicines, have helped power Merck’s growth—though its share price has not seen as much of a lift as some competitors'. In the race to find a vaccine for COVID-19, Merck has adopted a slow pace compared to others in the industry. Rather than tout the company’s progress, CEO Kenneth Frazier has instead criticized industry “hype” and has warned that the process for developing an effective vaccine could take years

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The pharma giant had a banner year in 2019, climbing seven slots on the Fortune 500. Revenue rose almost 11%, to $46.8 billion, while profits leaped 58%, to $9.8 billion. Blockbuster cancer drug Keytruda, as well as an expanded line of animal medicines, have helped power Merck’s growth—though its share price has not seen as much of a lift as some competitors'. More recently, Merck has been notably quiet in medical chatter about the novel coronavirus. But executives on a late April earnings call announced that the company has teams scanning its portfolio of antiviral candidates and vaccine assets for potential treatments.

companyRankingLists.description: As we face unprecedented collective challenges, cooperation has become a business superpower.
companyRankingLists.title: Change the World
companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Merck has doubled down on “impact” investing—taking stakes in smaller companies that aim to generate a measurable social good. Its portfolio currently commits about $39 million to entities working on projects including diagnostics, drug and vaccine R&D, and health infrastructure. It’s a future play with present benefits: Merck estimates more than 9 million people benefited from its impact portfolio in 2019.
